as_told.title: NASA study of Alcubierre's warp model

plain: The story is that NASA, the US space agency, has quietly paid for research into warp drive, an idea for crossing space faster than normal by bending space itself. A former intelligence official named Eric Haseltine talks about NASA's "innovative propulsion program," which he calls "fantastic." He does not say where his knowledge comes from, though he connects it to a work called The Shadow of Time. Michels tells his own version without naming a source. He says a man named Miguel Alcubierre came up with a theoretical model for such a drive, and that NASA has been studying it for years. He names Harold "Sonny" White, who he says has done interesting work on it at NASA. Neither man gives details of the program itself, such as its budget or what it built. The two tellers are independent, a former official and the host. If true, it would mean the government takes faster-than-light travel seriously enough to pay for it.
